correctness.rationale: The block-incidence graph is a tree; hence each nonroot vertex has a unique parent and lies in a uniquely determined sibling clique under that parent. Stable colour fixes the distance from the unique landmark and, through same-layer neighbour multiplicities, reveals its entire sibling-clique colour signature. The child colour counts divided by the signature multiplicity recover the number of each forward clique type. Reverse-depth induction reconstructs attached rooted descendant graphs from colours, after which independent sibling-clique and child-subtree permutations provide actual root-fixing automorphisms within every stable colour class. This gives within-graph orbit exactness for all finite connected block graphs and arbitrary additional vertex precolours. The eight-vertex two-triangles-linked-by-three-edges example has equitable degree cells but three automorphism orbits, showing unmarked refinement can fail. One-vertex graph and edge blocks included.

value.rationale: Block graphs are a canonical nontrivial extension of rooted trees, and a single individualization repairing orbit non-refinability for the entire class is a substantive structural boundary. The proof recovers clique-block multiplicities from ordinary vertex refinement without revealing the blocks, useful for graph algorithms and combinatorial logic.
